contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md requires coding standards, tests, review, and CI checks.
dco_justification: The project does not currently require a DCO or CLA. The MIT license and cryptographically signed commits do not by themselves satisfy this criterion. Adopting a contribution-rights mechanism requires an explicit maintainer decision. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md
governance_justification: https://docs.artemis.tum.de/about/governance documents roles, decisions, review, appointments, and dispute handling.
roles_responsibilities_justification: https://docs.artemis.tum.de/about/governance names maintainers by goal and module; https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/CODEOWNERS maps source ownership.
access_continuity_justification: The project maintainer confirmed that at least two active maintainers can independently manage issues, merge changes, publish releases, and recover essential project accounts within one week if any person becomes unavailable. https://docs.artemis.tum.de/about/governance#project-continuity
bus_factor_justification: Multiple active maintainers share development, review, merge, and release responsibilities. The maintainer confirmed independent continuity access for at least two people. https://docs.artemis.tum.de/about/governance
documentation_roadmap_justification: https://docs.artemis.tum.de/about/roadmap defines the October 2026–October 2027 direction and non-goals, links the public board, and requires extending the horizon before it expires. The maintainer approved this scope.
documentation_architecture_justification: https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/system-design describes the application architecture and deployment boundaries.
documentation_security_justification: https://docs.artemis.tum.de/about/trust and https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/SECURITY.md distinguish platform guarantees from operator responsibilities and unsupported uses.
documentation_quick_start_justification: https://docs.artemis.tum.de/about/try provides a quick start; https://docs.artemis.tum.de/student/getting-started/ covers initial learning workflows.
documentation_current_justification: Documentation is version-controlled with the implementation, built in CI, and required to change alongside affected behavior. https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/documentation
documentation_achievements_justification: https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/README.md links the current OpenSSF Best Practices badge and Scorecard. New public recognitions must be linked within 48 hours.
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The project targets WCAG 2.2 AA, uses accessible TUM AET UI primitives, enforces template accessibility rules, and documents keyboard, screen-reader, zoom, and contrast checks. Known gaps and the absence of certification are explicit. https://docs.artemis.tum.de/about/trust#accessibility
internationalization_justification: The Angular client uses translation keys with English and German translations; CI checks key consistency. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/i18n/
sites_password_security_justification: Internal accounts use configurable salted bcrypt via PasswordService; external identity providers can own authentication instead. Documentation is static and the repository/download site uses GitHub authentication. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/src/main/java/de/tum/cit/aet/artemis/account/service/user/PasswordService.java
maintenance_or_update_justification: https://docs.artemis.tum.de/about/releases documents supported versions, upgrade steps, automatic database migrations, and backports on request.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: The project maintainer confirmed that all reports resolved during the preceding twelve months were publicly credited unless the reporter requested anonymity. The security policy requires this credit in published advisories. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/SECURITY.md#disclosure-and-advisories
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/SECURITY.md#disclosure-and-advisories documents private triage, draft advisories, fixes, coordinated publication, and reporter credit.
coding_standards_justification: https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/ and https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md require the server, client, testing, and documentation conventions.
coding_standards_enforced_justification: CI runs Spotless, Checkstyle, Modernizer, ArchUnit, ESLint, Prettier, Stylelint, TypeScript, and repository-specific gates. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/workflows/ci-quality.yml
build_standard_variables_justification: The Artemis application is built as JVM bytecode and a JavaScript client, not native executables compiled by a project-owned C/C++ toolchain. Exercise templates are teaching material executed separately.
build_preserve_debug_justification: Java compilation retains debug information and the client build has configurable source maps. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/build.gradle and https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/angular.json
build_non_recursive_justification: Gradle orchestrates the server and explicit client/SBOM tasks; the Angular workspace builds the UI library before its consumer. These dependencies form an explicit task graph. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/build.gradle
build_repeatable_justification: Two complete builds of efdb52e01c3565a12f3d9bf2816466e6b4cea5eb on 2026-10-16 regenerated client/server/SBOM outputs after clearing Angular cache and bypassing Gradle cache. Both full WARs have SHA-256 f0f91909df8831a0bfe7f5ce8a6595eed3db3ac5edabef9bce73c27da2c2547e. Environment and commands: https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/best-practices#verified-build-pair
installation_common_justification: Container deployment uses standard Docker Compose operations; manual JVM deployment is also documented. https://docs.artemis.tum.de/admin/production-setup/
installation_standard_variables_justific: There is no project-owned POSIX make-install system or native install prefix. Deployment uses a JVM artifact or container with configurable mounts and configuration files. https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/docker-compose
installation_development_quick_justifica: https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/setup documents pinned toolchains, dependency installation, server/client startup, and test execution.
external_dependencies_justification: Gradle dependency declarations, pnpm lockfiles, and CycloneDX SBOMs identify dependencies in machine-readable form. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/build.gradle and https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/pnpm-lock.yaml
dependency_monitoring_justification: Renovate, Dependabot/Mend checks, and the running-instance OSV scanner monitor dependencies. Findings are assessed and mitigated, not hidden; the development-tool braces finding remains reported after a bounded local mitigation. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/SECURITY.md#dependency-and-supply-chain-security
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Dependency versions, locks, patches, and update procedures are version-controlled; Renovate proposes updates. https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/builds-and-dependencies
interfaces_current_justification: Guidelines require supported signal APIs, current Java/Angular versions, and TUM AET UI in place of deprecated controls. Architecture/lint rules enforce migrations and obsolete code is removed. https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/client-development
automated_integration_testing_justificat: CI runs on develop pushes and produces JUnit, Vitest, and Playwright reports. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/workflows/ci.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: Audit on 2026-10-16 of merged PRs labelled bug or bugfix since 2026-04-16 found 70 fixes: 59 changed test files and 57 added test/expect/assert constructs in their test diffs (81.4%). Review the linked fixes and reassess the rolling interval. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged+merged%3A%3E%3D2026-04-16+label%3Abug%2Cbugfix
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Successful complete CI run 38921395454 reports client statements 92.04% (83046/90220) and server JaCoCo instruction coverage 89.58%; server line coverage is 89.31%. Java uses instruction coverage as its statement proxy; the weighted README line badge is not this evidence. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/actions/runs/38921395454
test_policy_mandated_justification: https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md requires automated tests for new functionality and links module test guidance.
tests_documented_added_justification: https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md and https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/development-process require tests with change proposals and pull requests.
warnings_strict_justification: Compiler checks, strict TypeScript/template compilation, ESLint, Checkstyle, Modernizer, and architecture gates are applied in CI. Some existing deprecation warnings remain visible rather than being suppressed. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/workflows/ci-quality.yml
implement_secure_design_justification: https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/security-assurance connects least privilege, trust boundaries, input handling, isolation, and supply-chain controls to implementation and tests.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Authentication uses bcrypt password hashes, HS512 JWT signatures with startup key-length checks, and maintained TLS/WebAuthn libraries. Non-security cache fingerprints do not supply authentication or integrity guarantees. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/SECURITY.md
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: WebAuthn and TLS use maintained implementations supporting multiple signature/cipher algorithms rather than a project-owned cipher implementation. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/SECURITY.md#authentication
crypto_credential_agility_justification: Operators can provide and rotate authentication secrets and private-key file locations through external configuration without recompilation. https://docs.artemis.tum.de/admin/production-setup/security
crypto_used_network_justification: HTTPS and SSH are supported, and operators must protect external traffic. Some distributed deployment links use plaintext protocols inside an operator-controlled private network; secure deployment requires isolation or additional TLS termination. This exception is documented rather than claiming universal TLS defaults. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/SECURITY.md#infrastructure-and-transport-security
crypto_tls12_justification: Supported Java/Node runtimes and the documented production TLS configuration support TLS 1.2 and later; external reverse-proxy TLS configuration remains the operator responsibility. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/src/main/resources/config/application-prod.yml
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: The standard HTTPS clients retain Java/runtime certificate validation; production HTTP factories do not install a trust-all verifier. Operators must configure valid trust chains. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/src/main/java/de/tum/cit/aet/artemis/core/config/RestTemplateConfiguration.java
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: HTTPS performs certificate and hostname verification during the TLS handshake before application HTTP headers are sent, using standard runtime verification. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/src/main/java/de/tum/cit/aet/artemis/core/config/RestTemplateConfiguration.java
signed_releases_justification: The release workflow signs artifact provenance and container images; verification instructions distinguish supported assets from older releases and retrospective endorsements. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release
version_tags_signed_justification: Cryptographically signed release tags are not a documented uniformly enforced practice. Artifact provenance is signed separately; a signed commit is not a signed tag. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release
input_validation_justification: Server-side typed contracts, Bean Validation, authorization, allowlists and operation-specific path/type/size limits constrain untrusted input. The assurance case identifies controls and tests without trusting client validation. https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/security-assurance#untrusted-input-and-common-implementation-weaknesses
hardening_justification: Production startup rejects published default credentials; security headers, restricted rendering profiles, build isolation, constrained file paths, and static analysis add defense in depth. https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/security-assurance
assurance_case_justification: https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/security-assurance states security requirements, threat actors, trust boundaries, controls for common weaknesses, test evidence, and operator assumptions.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: OpenGrep SAST scanning is configured through Codacy alongside CodeQL Java/TypeScript analysis; the repository also maintains PMD security rules. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.codacy.yaml and https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/config/pmd/ruleset.xml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The Artemis server and client are Java and TypeScript/JavaScript; the project-owned application does not contain memory-unsafe C/C++ code. Exercise samples are teaching inputs run in separate build environments, and externally maintained native runtime dependencies are outside project-owned code.
achieve_silver_justification: Silver was first achieved on 2026-10-17, as recorded by first_achieved_silver_at in https://www.bestpractices.dev/en/projects/14163.json . The roadmap, security assurance case, and verified repeatable-build evidence were published in https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/pull/14258 . The live assessment is 100%: https://www.bestpractices.dev/en/projects/14163/silver
contributors_unassociated_justification: Reviewed the preceding year (2025-10-19 through 2026-10-19). Benedikt Fein (University of Passau, GitHub b-fein) contributed non-trivial production-documentation and programming-exercise changes, including https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/pull/11583 and https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/pull/12661 . Eduard Frankford (University of Innsbruck, GitHub eduardfrankford) contributed the websocket deadlock fix, lecture file-form improvements, and coverage-tooling correction: https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/pull/13834 , https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/pull/13965 , https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/pull/14243 . The maintainer confirmed these independent university affiliations on 2026-10-19; institutional staff listings corroborate them: https://www.fim.uni-passau.de/en/chair-for-software-engineering-ii/team and https://www.uibk.ac.at/de/informatik/team/ . These are substantive contributions; the numerical indicators in the criterion are examples, not required minimums.
copyright_per_file_justification: Many project-owned Java and TypeScript source files currently have no per-file copyright notice. Inventory authorship and exceptions before adding notices; do not replace existing third-party notices. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/src/main/java/
license_per_file_justification: The repository has an MIT LICENSE, but source files do not uniformly carry a license statement or SPDX identifier. Generated source needs a generator-level solution. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/LICENSE
repo_distributed_justification: The public repository uses Git with complete clone/fork support. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis
small_tasks_justification: The good first issue label identifies tasks for new contributors, and CONTRIBUTING links it. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22
require_2FA_justification: The authenticated GitHub organization API still reported two_factor_requirement_enabled=false for ls1intum on 2026-10-19. No alternative policy or control requiring 2FA for every central-repository and private-vulnerability-report user has been verified. Individual accounts using 2FA do not establish a mandatory requirement. Coordinate any enforcement change with the authorized organization administrators; this assessment does not change account access. https://github.com/ls1intum
secure_2FA_justification: Verify cryptographic second factors (passkeys/security keys or TOTP) rather than SMS-only access for everyone with repository or private-report access; organization-wide 2FA enforcement is not yet enabled.
code_review_standards_justification: Contribution and reviewer guidelines document author tasks, four-reviewer expectations, feature-maintainer approval, final review, and CI readiness. https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/reviewer-guidelines and https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md
two_person_review_justification: The 2026-10-19 OpenSSF Scorecard scan at merged revision 3d0bd7dfb4cd077394cc7cc22293855ed0dad9d5 found 27 of 30 changesets approved by reviewers, above the 50% threshold (Code-Review 9/10; overall Scorecard 9.0). An independent check of the 28 PR merges among the latest 30 first-parent commits found 27 had a non-author human approval before merge, including all three coverage PRs. This records recent practice; reassess the preceding release interval when updating the criterion. https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/ls1intum/Artemis ; https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/pull/14286 ; https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/pull/14280 ; https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/pull/14279
build_reproducible_justification: On 2026-10-19 the project maintainer confirmed that another maintainer independently built the same source revision in a separate build and obtained the identical complete WAR SHA-256. This records the maintainer attestation of independent bit-for-bit reproduction. The documented release-build procedure regenerates the production client, compiled server and bundled SBOMs using -Preproducible, frozen dependencies, controlled toolchain inputs and no reused build output: https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/best-practices#repeatable-builds . Implementation and the earlier controlled-environment build pair are documented in https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/pull/14258 . The earlier same-checkout pair establishes repeatability; the separately confirmed independent rebuild supplies the Gold evidence. A container image is one possible way to describe a build environment, not a mandatory form of this criterion.
test_invocation_justification: The standard Gradle wrapper test and pnpm Vitest commands are documented. https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/setup
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The CI workflow tests pull requests and protected-branch pushes and publishes test reports. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_statement_coverage90_justification: Client Vitest statements are 92.06% (82,875/90,018) in successful complete CI https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/actions/runs/39163316687 ; the client production sources are unchanged between that tested revision and merged develop 3d0bd7dfb4cd077394cc7cc22293855ed0dad9d5. The successful full seven-shard server run for merged PR #14286 reports 91.98% JaCoCo instructions, the Java statement proxy: https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/actions/runs/39164068412 . Recombining the passing seven-shard execution data from that run and the other two merged test PRs (https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/actions/runs/39163868255 and https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/actions/runs/39160461237) against the merged production classes gives 534,108/577,958 instructions (92.41%) and 99,314/107,851 lines (92.08%), with the existing exclusions. This recombines complete passing server suites. Run 39160461237 failed its programming-assessment E2E case, although all seven server shards passed; only those passing server data contribute to coverage. Its client job was skipped, so client coverage comes from CI 39163316687. This is not a new standalone develop run or a claim that every source workflow passed. The weighted README line badge is not used as statement evidence.
test_branch_coverage80_justification: Client Vitest branches are 80.19% (33,791/42,138) in successful complete CI https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/actions/runs/39163316687 ; client production sources match merged develop 3d0bd7dfb4cd077394cc7cc22293855ed0dad9d5. The successful full seven-shard server run for merged PR #14286 reports 38,456/47,889 branches (80.30%): https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/actions/runs/39164068412 . Recombining passing seven-shard execution data from that run plus https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/actions/runs/39163868255 and https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/actions/runs/39160461237 against the merged production classes gives 38,842/47,897 branches (81.09%). All seven server shards passed in each input run. Run 39160461237 failed programming-assessment E2E overall; only its passing server-suite data are used. The recomputation preserves the existing exclusions and is not a new standalone CI run. Both language suites clear the 80% threshold.
hardened_site_justification: Rechecked HTTPS GET responses on 2026-10-19. https://artemis.tum.de/ now returns HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, and a Content-Security-Policy. However, https://docs.artemis.tum.de/ returns none of those four headers. Gold explicitly requires the headers even for a fully static website. Add appropriate response headers at the documentation hosting/proxy layer and recheck project, repository and download endpoints before marking Met.
security_review_justification: On 2026-10-19 the project maintainer confirmed that the core maintainer team conducts monthly internal human security reviews, including the security requirements and trust boundaries. This is within the preceding five years. The requirements, boundaries, operator assumptions and control argument are documented at https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/security-assurance and https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/.github/SECURITY.md#security-audits-and-open-source-transparency . The confirmation concerns human review; the assurance document and automated scans alone are not claimed as substitutes. Confidential review findings need not be disclosed in this public entry.
dynamic_analysis_justification: On 2026-10-19 the project maintainer confirmed that, before every proposed major production release, maintainers require successful complete server and client test runs for the release candidate, review runtime failures and coverage, and resolve significant findings before release. Both automated suites exceed 80% branch coverage, qualifying as dynamic-analysis tools under this criterion. Server complete passing CI: https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/actions/runs/39164068412 ; client complete passing CI: https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/actions/runs/39163316687 . Coverage and runtime-assertion evidence: https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/pull/14289 . This records the human pre-release review practice; the release: published workflow is not used to prove analysis before publication. Fuzzing remains outside the current scope.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Delivered server code contains hundreds of Bean Validation runtime contracts on request DTOs and domain objects, Spring Assert guards, and explicit constructor/invariant checks such as WorkerSettings. These checks execute during tests and reject invalid state; they are not merely assertions in test code. JUnit exercises valid and invalid inputs and failure paths. The Gradle test task was inspected on 2026-10-19: enableAssertions=true and allJvmArgs includes -ea, also enabling Java language assertions. https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/gradle/test.gradle ; https://docs.gradle.org/current/dsl/org.gradle.api.tasks.testing.Test.html#org.gradle.api.tasks.testing.Test:enableAssertions ; https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/src/main/java/de/tum/cit/aet/artemis/aiworker/config/WorkerSettings.java ; https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/blob/develop/src/test/java/de/tum/cit/aet/artemis/aiworker/api/WorkerBoundaryContractsTest.java . Full successful CI for the expanded tests is https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/actions/runs/39164068412 . Production JVM assertion policy is a separate operator choice.
